headings.title: Transfer of transportation quasi-judicial duties to judges
headings.reviewNote: Transfers quasi-judicial transportation duties from public service commissioners to administrative law judges while leaving ministerial duties to the division.

headings.title: Judge powers, rulemaking concurrence, and relaxed evidence rules
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes each judge to exercise division powers individually (requiring unanimous judge concurrence for rulemaking), provides for rules governing hearings except under section 622.035, and exempts proceedings from technical rules of evidence.

headings.title: Docket fee collection and deposit into highway fund
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the division may charge a reasonable docket fee set by rule for non-staff filings, payable to the director of revenue for deposit into the state highway fund.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections of 622.030 (effective 7-01-85; archived cross-reference notes transfer of division ALJs to AHC under § 226.008); refined ministerial-duty and rulemaking-concurrence details.

headings.title: Prohibition on employment solicitation, passes, and gifts
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits division judges and employees from soliciting employment recommendations from regulated carriers and prohibits regulated entities or their personnel from offering offices, free passes/carriage, fare reductions, gifts, entertainment, or gratuities.

headings.title: Mandatory removal from office and public officer status
headings.reviewNote: Requires removal from office of any division judge or employee violating this section and deems all division judges and employees to be public officers.

headings.title: Civil penalty up to twenty thousand dollars against carriers
headings.reviewNote: Subjects violating carriers or regulated persons to an attorney-general civil action for up to $20,000 in civil penalties (in addition to other penalties), credited to the public school fund.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalty for division or carrier personnel
headings.reviewNote: Classifies violations by any officer, agent, or employee of the division or of any carrier as a misdemeanor punishable by up to a $1,000 fine, up to one year in county jail, or both.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections of 622.130; added public-officer status in subsection 2, public school fund crediting in subsection 3, and fine/jail limits in subsection 4.

headings.title: Conferences with state and federal transportation commissions
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the division may confer in person, by correspondence, or at conventions with other states' and federal railroad, transportation, or utility agencies on matters relating to its duties.

headings.title: Cooperative agreements and deposit of grants in railroad expense fund
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes cooperative agreements or agency relationships with federal or other state transportation commissions regarding railroads/street railroads (as limited by section 622.110) and requires depositing received grants or financial assistance in the section 622.015 railroad expense fund.

headings.title: Joint investigations, hearings, and concurrent orders
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the division to conduct joint investigations, hold joint hearings within or without Missouri, and issue joint or concurrent orders with federal or other state agencies.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections of 622.140; realigned shifted subsections 1-3 and corrected grant deposit destination from fabricated highway fund to the section 622.015 railroad expense fund.

headings.title: Authority to establish uniform system of accounts
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the division may establish a system of accounts and record forms for railroads, street railroads, and common carriers (giving at least six months' notice of alterations) conforming as nearly as may be to Interstate Commerce Commission standards.

headings.title: Division access to and inspection of carrier accounts
headings.reviewNote: Grants the division constant access to carrier accounts, records, and memoranda and authorizes designated officers or employees under division order to inspect and examine them.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections of 622.190; added six-month alteration notice and ICC conformity detail in subsection 1.

headings.title: Annual verified report by railroads and street railroads
headings.reviewNote: Requires every railroad and street railroad to file an annual report with the division verified under oath by a specified corporate official or responsible person.

headings.title: Prescription and June thirtieth furnishing of report forms
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division to prescribe report forms and contents and furnish blank forms to each covered corporation and person on or before June thirtieth annually.

headings.title: Optional reporting of intrastate rates, fares, and contracts
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the division may require reports to include information on intrastate fare or freight rates, regulations, agreements, or contracts.

headings.title: Notification to amend defective or erroneous reports
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division to notify a corporation or person to amend any defective or believed-erroneous report within a division-prescribed time.

headings.title: Preservation of original sworn reports in division office
headings.reviewNote: Requires preserving the subscribed and sworn original reports in the office of the division.

headings.title: Periodic reports and specific answers to division questions
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the division may require periodic reports and specific answers to questions on matters where it needs information.

headings.title: September thirtieth filing deadline and sixty-day extension
headings.reviewNote: Requires common carrier corporations to file annual reports on or before September thirtieth each year and provides the division may extend the deadline by up to sixty days.

headings.title: One-hundred-dollar daily forfeiture credited to public school fund
headings.reviewNote: Imposes a $100-per-day forfeiture for failure to file, amend, or answer required reports, recoverable by division action and deposited to the public school fund.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 8 subsections of 622.200; realigned shifted subsections 2-8 and corrected annual deadline from fabricated March 31 to September 30.

headings.title: Written entry and optional county recording of division orders
headings.reviewNote: Requires every division order, authorization, or certificate to be in writing and entered on division records, and authorizes recording certified copies (and non-modification certificates) in county or city recorder offices to impart notice.

headings.title: Intrastate carrier duty to make records available in state
headings.reviewNote: Requires every common carrier engaging in intrastate commerce in Missouri to make all legally kept accounts, records, memoranda, books, and papers available to the division within the state.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections of 622.210; added county-recording notice provision in subsection 1 and in-state availability requirement in subsection 2.

headings.title: Fee exemptions, publication charges, and monthly remittance
headings.reviewNote: Exempts public officers (official capacity) and ordinary distribution of division annual reports from copy fees, authorizes reasonable charges for division publications, and requires monthly remittance of collected fees to the director of revenue.

headings.title: Deposit of fees into division fund to offset copy expenses
headings.reviewNote: Requires depositing collected fees to the credit of the division fund from which copy-furnishing expenses are paid, to offset those expenses.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections of 622.230; replaced fabricated certified-copy schedule in subsection 1 and corrected deposit destination in subsection 2 from highway fund to the expense-paying division fund.

headings.title: Authority to require safety devices and emergency orders
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the division may, after hearing, order carriers to maintain/operate facilities safely and install appropriate safety devices, and may waive prior notice and hearing when imminent threat of serious harm exists (with prompt post-order hearing opportunity).

headings.title: Prohibition on unshielded red signs along main line tracks
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits unshielded red neon or other red signs or lights along or in the line of vision of main line railroad tracks where they may confuse locomotive crews, and requires division inspection and shield prescriptions upon complaint.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections of 622.240; added emergency waiver/post-order hearing procedure in subsection 1 and complaint inspection/shielding rule in subsection 2.

headings.title: General supervision over common carriers
headings.reviewNote: Grants the division general supervision over all common carriers and requires examining them to stay informed of service safety, adequacy, security, and legal compliance.

headings.title: Inspection of carrier property, tracks, and locomotive riding
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes division inspectors or employees to enter and inspect carrier property, equipment, tracks, and facilities, ride in-service locomotives or trains, and upon good cause and reasonable notice use an inspection locomotive, car, or high-rail vehicle.

headings.title: Examination of carrier records and subpoena duces tecum
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the division and ALJs upon notice to examine pertinent books, contracts, records, and papers under this chapter and chapters 387–391, and to compel production by subpoena duces tecum or require sworn copies.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections of 622.250; added locomotive-riding authority in subsection 2 and subpoena duces tecum/sworn-copy authority in subsection 3.

headings.title: Division investigations on own motion or for violations
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the division to investigate any carrier act or omission on its own motion and requires inquiry into any violation of law or division order or decision.

headings.title: Written complaints, forwarding, reparation, and investigation
headings.reviewNote: Allows aggrieved persons or corporations to file written complaints, requires forwarding to the carrier (optionally with an order to satisfy or answer), terminates action upon timely reparation and cessation, and requires investigation upon reasonable grounds if unsatisfied.

headings.title: Sixty-day deadline to file order after final submission
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division, within sixty days after final submission of a complaint investigation, to make and file an order dismissing the complaint or directing the carrier to satisfy it.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections of 622.260; realigned forwarding/reparation into subsection 2 and captured the 60-day final order deadline in subsection 3.

headings.title: Mandamus and injunction actions by division general counsel
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division to direct its general counsel to sue in circuit court for mandamus or injunctive relief (including TROs, preliminary, and permanent orders) to stop or prevent carrier violations or threatened violations.

headings.title: Thirty-day answer limit and summary judicial inquiry
headings.reviewNote: Requires the court to set an answer period not exceeding thirty days after service where contemplated by court rules, and upon default or answer to inquire immediately into the facts without formal pleadings or technical requirements.

headings.title: Joinder of necessary or proper parties
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes joining other persons or corporations deemed necessary or proper to make orders, judgments, or writs effective upon application of the division's general counsel.

headings.title: Final judgment dismissing action or granting writ or injunction
headings.reviewNote: Directs final judgment either dismissing the action or issuing a writ of mandamus, injunction, or both as prayed for or in modified form affording appropriate relief.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections of 622.290; corrected answer deadline in subsection 2 from fabricated 20 days to not exceeding 30 days and removed fabricated appellate-review clause from subsection 4.

headings.title: Annual estimation of division railroad regulatory expenses
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division before each fiscal year beginning July 1, 1997, to estimate expenses attributable to regulating railroads and street railroads, separately estimating direct and indirect expenses.

headings.title: Revenue-based allocation, three-percent cap, and mileage adjustments
headings.reviewNote: Allocates and assesses estimated expenses by preceding-year gross intrastate operating revenues, capped at 3% of total gross intrastate operating revenues and adjusted by route-mile minimums and caps ($100–$500 for <50 miles; >=$1,000 for 50–100 miles; >=$5,000 for >100 miles).

headings.title: July first assessment statement and payment schedule
headings.reviewNote: Requires mailing written statements by July first, payable in full by July fifteenth or in four equal installments (July 15, October 15, January 15, April 15) to the director of revenue for remittance to the state treasurer.

headings.title: Railroad expense fund credit, nonreversion, and assessment reduction
headings.reviewNote: Requires crediting payments to the section 622.015 railroad expense fund, bars reversion to general revenue, and applies unexpended year-end balances to reduce succeeding-year assessments proportionally by group.

headings.title: Annual March thirty-first sworn intrastate revenue statement
headings.reviewNote: Requires covered railroads and street railroads to file sworn gross intrastate operating revenue statements within ten days after August 28, 1996, and by March thirty-first annually thereafter, with binding division estimates upon failure to file.

headings.title: Inapplicability to chapter 390 motor carriers
headings.reviewNote: Excludes chapter 390 motor carriers and motor-carrier regulatory expenses from this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 6 subsections of 622.300; added July 1, 1997 start, 3%/mileage caps, installment dates, railroad expense fund credit, and August 28, 1996/March 31 filing dates.

headings.title: Public records status of formal division proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Declares all formal proceedings of the division and all documents and records filed in their official records to be public records.

headings.title: Hearings on pending legislation and legislative recommendations
headings.reviewNote: Requires conducting hearings and reporting conclusions on pending legislation within division jurisdiction when requested by the general assembly, either house, or the governor, and provides the division may recommend legislation in the public interest.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections of 622.310; verified alignment and preserved permissive legislative recommendation authority in subsection 2.

headings.title: Parties authorized to file written complaints
headings.reviewNote: Allows the division on its own motion or any person, corporation, commercial/civic association, or body politic/municipality to file a written complaint alleging violations of law or division rules, orders, or decisions.

headings.title: Joinder of claims and bar on misjoinder motions
headings.reviewNote: Permits joining all complaint matters in one hearing and bars motions for misjoinder of causes or misjoinder/nonjoinder of parties both before the division and on judicial review.

headings.title: Absence of direct damage and service of complaint
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the division need not dismiss a complaint for absence of direct damage to the complainant and requires serving a copy on the subject carrier, corporation, or person.

headings.title: Manner of service of process and notices
headings.reviewNote: Permits service in division proceedings personally or by prepaid mail upon persons eligible for civil summons service, and authorizes the division or its employees in official capacity to serve process and notices.

headings.title: Ten-day hearing notice and public-necessity exception
headings.reviewNote: Requires fixing the hearing time and place and serving notice at least ten days beforehand unless the division finds public necessity requires an earlier date.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 5 subsections of 622.320; corrected subsection 4 to prepaid mail (not certified mail) and added the public-necessity exception in subsection 5.

headings.title: Right to be heard, intervention, and witness process
headings.reviewNote: Entitles complainants, respondents, and division-approved intervenors to be heard and introduce evidence at hearings, and requires the division to issue process enforcing attendance of necessary witnesses.

headings.title: Written investigation reports and civil-style depositions
headings.reviewNote: Requires written reports stating conclusions and orders after division investigations, and authorizes the division, ALJs, or any party to take in-state or out-of-state depositions and compel document production with circuit-court witness and officer fees.

headings.title: Additional time and extensions for order compliance
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the division may grant more than thirty days to comply with an order when reasonably necessary and may extend compliance deadlines on application for good cause shown.

headings.title: Complete formal hearing record and unanimous transcript waiver
headings.reviewNote: Requires a full record of formal hearings taken by a division-appointed reporter, entitles parties to be heard in person or by attorney, and permits waiving printed transcript preparation by unanimous party consent.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections of 622.340; verified alignment and added witness process in subsection 1 and 30-day threshold in subsection 3.

headings.title: Subpoena issuance, statewide service, and state-paid fees
headings.reviewNote: Requires subpoenas to be signed and issued by an ALJ or the director, extends them statewide, permits service by court process servers or designated adult persons, and pays circuit-court witness and service fees from state funds on sworn approved vouchers.

headings.title: Party liability for fees, demand at service, and free-transport rule
headings.reviewNote: Assigns service and witness fees to the summoning party, excuses non-division-paid witnesses from attending if demanded travel and one-day attendance fees are not paid/tendered at service, and bars mileage for witnesses given free transportation.

headings.title: Fee-free certified copies and filings by public officers
headings.reviewNote: Requires public officers to furnish certified copies of filed documents to the division without charge and bars charging the division or public counsel any entering, filing, docketing, or recording fees.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections of 622.360; added free-transportation mileage bar in subsection 2 and public-counsel filing-fee exemption in subsection 3.

headings.title: Service of certified copies of division orders
headings.reviewNote: Requires serving every division order on every affected person or corporation by personal delivery or prepaid mailing of a certified copy.

headings.title: Immediate written receipt notice and acceptance statement
headings.reviewNote: Requires recipients to immediately notify the division in writing of receipt (signed and acknowledged by an authorized officer for corporations) and, if required by the order, state within the specified time whether its terms are accepted and will be obeyed.

headings.title: Thirty-day effective date and continuing force of orders
headings.reviewNote: Makes every division order or decision effective thirty days after service (except as otherwise provided) and keeps it in force for its designated period or until changed or abrogated, unless unauthorized by law or unconstitutional.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections of 622.410; added the 30-day effective date in subsection 3.

headings.title: Application for rehearing and thirty-day determination
headings.reviewNote: Allows any interested carrier, corporation, or person to apply for rehearing, requires granting it if sufficient reason appears, and requires determining granted rehearings within thirty days after final submission.

headings.title: Mandatory pre-effective-date rehearing and specificity of grounds
headings.reviewNote: Bars any court action unless a rehearing application was filed before the order's effective date, requires setting forth specific grounds of alleged unlawfulness or unreasonableness, and bars raising unstated grounds in court.

headings.title: No automatic excuse or stay of order enforcement
headings.reviewNote: Provides that applying for rehearing does not excuse compliance or stay enforcement of a division order except as directed by division order.

headings.title: Abrogation or modification of orders after rehearing
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the division to abrogate, change, or modify an unjust or unwarranted order after rehearing, giving the new order original-order force without affecting rights arising under the original order.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections of 622.420; moved the court-review prerequisite and before-effective-date deadline from subsection 1 to subsection 2.

headings.title: Circuit court stay notice, findings, and suspending bond
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies a writ of review does not automatically stay an order, authorizes discretionary circuit court stays only after three days' notice, hearing, and specific evidence-based findings of great or irreparable damage, and requires an approved suspending bond payable to the state.

headings.title: Impoundment of excess rate collections in court or trust
headings.reviewNote: Requires a circuit court staying a rate-affecting order to direct impounding excess collections into court or an interest-bearing bank or trust company pending final decision.

headings.title: Verified accounting of overcharges and street-railroad receipt rule
headings.reviewNote: Requires carriers staying rate-lowering passenger or household-goods motor vehicle orders to keep sworn accounts of excess charges and refundable payor names/addresses (exempting street railroads from name/address logs if they issue division-approved printed receipts).

headings.title: Court authority to require additional suspending bond security
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the court may from time to time require additional security or an increased suspending bond when necessary to secure prompt payment of damages or overcharges.

headings.title: Prompt refund of excess moneys and interest upon decision
headings.reviewNote: Requires prompt payment of excess collected moneys plus any trust interest to entitled parties upon the circuit court's decision, unless an appeal is granted.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 5 subsections of 622.440; moved the suspending bond requirement into subsection 1, aligned impoundment in subsection 2, and added the street-railroad receipt exception in subsection 3.

headings.title: Appellate review procedure and record on appeal
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the division and participating parties to appeal circuit court review judgments to Missouri appellate courts as in civil cases, with the division-certified transcript/exhibits plus the circuit court transcript constituting the record on appeal.

headings.title: Immediate docket placement and precedence over other civil causes
headings.reviewNote: Requires appellate clerks to immediately place appeals on the pending-term docket with precedence over all civil causes of a different nature.

headings.title: Circuit court discretion to suspend judgment pending appeal
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the circuit court in its discretion to suspend its judgment pending appeal upon filing of a sufficient bond and compliance with all statutory suspension conditions.

headings.title: Application of general appellate laws
headings.reviewNote: Applies general laws governing appeals to the supreme court and court of appeals so far as applicable and not conflicting with chapter 622.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections of 622.450; corrected subsection 3 from appellate-court to circuit-court discretion to suspend judgment on bond.

headings.title: Civil penalty of one hundred to two thousand dollars
headings.reviewNote: Subjects any carrier, corporation, or person violating the constitution, law, or a division order where no other penalty is provided to a penalty of $100 to $2,000 per offense.

headings.title: Each violation and continuing day as separate offense
headings.reviewNote: Deems every violation, and each day of a continuing violation, to be a separate and distinct offense.

headings.title: Imputation of officer, agent, or employee acts to carrier
headings.reviewNote: Deems the act, omission, or failure of any officer, agent, or employee acting within the scope of official employment duties to be that of the carrier, corporation, or person.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections of 622.480; verified alignment with archived source text.

headings.title: Intrastate skill performance evaluation certificates under 49 CFR 391.41
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the division may grant an intrastate-only skill performance evaluation certificate to a driver not physically qualified under 49 CFR 391.41, which the driver must carry while operating a commercial motor vehicle.

headings.title: Required application contents and treating physician statement
headings.reviewNote: Lists ten required application items, including driving experience, vehicle modifications, current CDL, medical examiner's certificate, treating physician's safety opinion, and any additional division-required medical exam or report.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority conditioned on no federal DOT sanctions
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division to promulgate rules for intrastate 49 CFR 391.41 certificates, implementable only if the U.S. Department of Transportation will not impose sanctions, including funding sanctions, against Missouri.

headings.title: Definition of skill performance evaluation certificate
headings.reviewNote: Defines skill performance evaluation certificate as division approval allowing a driver to operate commercial motor vehicles intrastate despite not meeting minimum federal interstate fitness standards.

headings.title: Chapter 536 compliance and nonseverability of rulemaking
headings.reviewNote: Subjects rules to chapter 536 and section 536.028, with nonseverability voiding post-August 28, 2002 rules if general assembly review powers are held unconstitutional.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 5 subsections of 622.555 (2002 H.B. 1270 & H.B. 2032); replaced fabricated driving-exam and 2-year-term headings in subsections 3-4 with USDOT-sanction-conditioned rulemaking and statutory definition.

headings.title: Definitions for property carrier registration sections
headings.reviewNote: Defines division (renamed division of motor carrier and railroad safety after June 30, 1997), household goods, property carrier registration, and registered property carrier for sections 622.600 to 622.620.

headings.title: Cross-application of definitions with section 390.020
headings.reviewNote: Applies section 622.600 definitions to chapter 390 and chapter 622, and applies section 390.020 and chapter 622 definitions to sections 622.600 to 622.620 except where context requires otherwise.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections of 622.600; corrected defined-term list in subsection 1 and bidirectional cross-application in subsection 2.

headings.title: Prohibition on regulating property carrier prices, routes, or services
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits the division from enforcing laws, rules, or orders relating to prices, routes, or services of intrastate property carriers, except for household goods, passengers, or as expressly authorized in sections 622.600 to 622.620.

headings.title: Applicability of non-preempted motor carrier powers and terminal enforcement
headings.reviewNote: Applies non-inconsistent division powers under chapters 386, 387, 390, and 622 to registered property carriers except as preempted by section 601 of the Federal Aviation Administration Authorization Act of 1994, including enforcing section 307.400 DPS rules only within terminals.

headings.title: Inapplicability of enumerated chapter 390 sections except household goods
headings.reviewNote: Exempts intrastate property transportation, except household goods under section 622.600, from sections 390.051, 390.061, 390.062, 390.081, and 390.111.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections of 622.602; replaced fabricated headings across all 3 subsections with the price/route/service deregulation rule, FAAAA 1994 preemption/terminal enforcement, and chapter 390 section exclusions.

headings.title: Voiding of pre-1995 intrastate property certificates with exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Voids certificates or permits issued before January 1, 1995, authorizing intrastate motor-vehicle property transport, except portions authorizing irregular-route household goods, intrastate passengers, or interstate commerce.

headings.title: Deemed qualification and issuance of registrations to active 1994 carriers
headings.reviewNote: Deems carriers holding active certificates/permits on December 31, 1994 (or issued under emergency rules thereafter) qualified as registered property carriers upon meeting licensing and insurance requirements without filing a section 622.608 application, with registrations issued within a reasonable time after August 28, 1996.

headings.title: Restriction on hazardous material transport to August 28, 1996 authority
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies the section does not authorize transporting Title 49 CFR hazardous materials beyond those expressly authorized on August 28, 1996, permits section 622.608 applications for additional hazardous materials, and preserves chapter 260 licensing duties.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections of 622.606; corrected inverted subsection 1 (pre-1995 property certificates are void, not grandfathered) and added December 31, 1994 and August 28, 1996 statutory dates.

headings.title: Verified application, liability insurance, vehicle fees, and safety compliance
headings.reviewNote: Requires perjury-verified applications accompanied by liability insurance/surety/self-insurance proof (section 390.126), vehicle license fee applications and payment (section 390.136), and safety and Title 49 CFR hazardous-materials compliance information.

headings.title: Judge review, twenty-day hearing, and forty-five-day approval rule
headings.reviewNote: Directs an ALJ to grant qualified applications without hearing, authorizes further investigation if inadequate, requires a hearing within twenty days of applicant request if opposed, and approves the application automatically if not determined within forty-five days after hearing close.

headings.title: Prohibition on commodity or route limits except household goods and hazmat
headings.reviewNote: Bars restricting registrations by commodity, route, or service except mandatory restrictions against household goods and against any Title 49 CFR hazardous material for which the applicant has not shown compliance.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections of 622.608; added 20-day hearing deadline and 45-day automatic-approval rule in subsection 2 and no-commodity/route-restriction rule in subsection 3.

headings.title: Division approval of joint property carrier registration transfer
headings.reviewNote: Permits transferring a property carrier registration in its entirety only with division approval, required when both transferor and transferee join in the prescribed application and the transferee meets all section 622.608 qualifications.

headings.title: Transfer restrictions on hazardous material transport authority
headings.reviewNote: Requires transferring the registration in its entirety except restricting against any previously authorized Title 49 CFR hazardous material unless the transferee proves compliance, while allowing a separate section 622.608 application for additional hazardous materials.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections of 622.610; verified alignment and preserved separate-application rule in subsection 2.

headings.title: Training requirements for enforcement personnel without chapter 590 mandate
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division by rule, notwithstanding section 390.045, to adopt reasonable training requirements for enforcement personnel without needing to require chapter 590 basic peace officer training.

headings.title: Rulemaking compliance with section 536.024
headings.reviewNote: Provides that no rule or portion of a rule promulgated under sections 622.600 to 622.620 becomes effective unless promulgated under section 536.024.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections of 622.620; verified alignment with archived source text.
